subproblems.title: Almost-everywhere measurability of the approximate tangent projection of an integer multiplicity triple (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be open, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n): M = R.carrier ⊆ U is Borel and countably n-rectifiable; θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]); ξ = R.orient is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; and for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q that ξ(x) orients. For x ∈ ℝ^P let p_x := (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection be the orthogonal projection onto the chosen approximate tangent plane T_xM of M at x (onto {0} if none exists). Then x ↦ p_x ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), with the Borel σ-algebra of the operator-norm topology, is almost-everywhere measurable with respect to μ_R := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → AEMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (not a proof step): this declaration is already comparator-accepted (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.mean_curvature_monotonicity-a1.tangent_projection_measurable-a1, candidate commit 7eb1db9), and the self-contained proof below is its accepted proof. In the selected node it supplies the measurability of x ↦ P_{T_xM} that step 1 of the supplied proof uses implicitly to integrate div_M X_ρ and |D^⊥r|². Source: Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 75–90); Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753: ξ orients T_xM "in an Hⁿ-measurable way").
One could argue through the orientation: P_{T_xM} is a continuous function of the unit simple n-vector ξ(x). Writing that function explicitly needs Cauchy–Binet identities, for which the pinned Mathlib has no support. So we prove the statement directly from the blow-up definition of T_xM, using only the fields of R. For U = ℝ^P one could use continuity of the blow-up integrals in x; here Tonelli measurability is used instead, so that U may be any open set.
Notation. M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, Hⁿ := μHE[n], ν := Hⁿ⌞M (μHE[n].restrict M), μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ. T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x, p_x := its starProjection, η_{x,λ}(y) := λ⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap x λ), and e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis.
0. Reduction to ν. μ = ν.withDensity θ ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so every ν-AEMeasurable function is μ-AEMeasurable (AEMeasurable.mono_ac). We show that x ↦ p_x is ν-AEMeasurable.
1. Case n = 0. If some Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M x Q, then T_x is such a Q (the chosen witness in the definition of approxTangentPlane). Its finrank is 0, so T_x = ⊥. Otherwise T_x = ⊥ by definition. So x ↦ p_x is constant, hence measurable. From now on assume n ≥ 1.
2. ν is σ-finite.
 (a) U is open, so U = ⋃_j K_j with K_j := {y : |y| ≤ j, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/(j+1)} compact and K_j ⊆ U. (If U = ℝ^P, take K_j := closedBall(0, j).)
 (b) θ ≥ 1 on M (R.mult_pos), so ν(K_j) = Hⁿ(M ∩ K_j) ≤ ∫_{M∩K_j} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
 (c) ν(ℝ^P ∖ U) = Hⁿ(M ∖ U) = 0, because M ⊆ U (R.carrier_subset).
 (d) So ℝ^P is a countable union of sets of finite ν-measure. Hence ν is σ-finite, in particular s-finite. In Lean this instance must be supplied by hand from (a)–(c); it is needed for step 6.
3. Tangent planes a.e. By R.orients, for ν-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. At such x, T_x is the chosen witness, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x T_x holds and finrank T_x = n. Let G be the set of these x; then ν(ℝ^P ∖ G) = 0.
4. Test functions. Let χ(t) := max(1 − t, 0), and for u ∈ ℝ^P let f_u(y) := χ(|y|²)⟨u, y⟩². f_u is continuous and ≥ 0 and vanishes outside closedBall(0, 1), so f_u ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
5. Integrals over n-planes. Claim: for every subspace Q with finrank Q = n, ∫_Q f_u dHⁿ = c_n|p_Q u|², where c_n := ∫_{ℝ^n} χ(|z|²) z₁² dz ∈ (0, ∞) (Lebesgue measure).
 (a) Take an orthonormal basis τ₁, …, τ_n of Q, and the linear isometry ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(z) = Σ_i z_i τ_i, whose range is Q. Then Hⁿ⌞Q is the push-forward of Hⁿ on ℝ^n under ι (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), and Hⁿ on ℝ^n is Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
 (b) With a_i := ⟨u, τ_i⟩, f_u(ι(z)) = χ(|z|²)(Σ_i a_i z_i)². So ∫_Q f_u dHⁿ = Σ_{i,j} a_i a_j ∫ χ(|z|²) z_i z_j dz.
 (c) For i ≠ j, the reflection z_i ↦ −z_i preserves Lebesgue measure and |z| and changes the sign of z_i z_j, so that integral is 0. For i = j, the coordinate swap z_i ↔ z₁ shows that the integral equals c_n.
 (d) Hence ∫_Q f_u dHⁿ = c_n Σ_i a_i² = c_n|p_Q u|². Finally c_n < ∞, since the integrand is continuous with compact support, and c_n > 0, since it is continuous, ≥ 0, and positive at (1/2, 0, …, 0).
6. Blow-up integrals are measurable in x. Fix u and λ > 0, and put Φ(x) := ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f_u dHⁿ, the integral appearing in HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.
 (a) f_u ≥ 0 is continuous, so Φ(x) = (∫⁻_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f_u dHⁿ).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae). This holds whether or not f_u is integrable there.
 (b) η_{x,λ} is a translation followed by multiplication by λ⁻¹, hence a homeomorphism, so η_{x,λ}(M) is Borel. Also Hⁿ(η_{x,λ}(B)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(B) for every B (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image for the translation, Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ for the dilation).
 (c) For Borel B, Hⁿ(B ∩ η_{x,λ}(M)) = Hⁿ(η_{x,λ}(η_{x,λ}⁻¹(B) ∩ M)) = λ^{−n}ν(η_{x,λ}⁻¹(B)). That is, Hⁿ⌞η_{x,λ}(M) = λ^{−n}(η_{x,λ})_*ν. Therefore ∫⁻_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f_u dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫⁻ f_u(λ⁻¹(y − x)) dν(y) (lintegral_map).
 (d) (x, y) ↦ f_u(λ⁻¹(y − x)) is continuous on ℝ^P × ℝ^P, hence measurable for the product σ-algebra (ℝ^P is second countable). Since ν is s-finite (step 2), x ↦ ∫⁻ f_u(λ⁻¹(y − x)) dν(y) is measurable (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'). Hence Φ is Borel measurable.
7. Limits.
 (a) Let λ_k := 1/(k+1), and let Φ_{u,k} be the function of step 6 with λ = λ_k.
 (b) For x ∈ G, apply HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x T_x to f_u, with λ_k → 0 through positive values. This gives Φ_{u,k}(x) → ∫_{T_x} f_u dHⁿ = c_n|p_x u|², by step 5 and finrank T_x = n.
 (c) ν-a.e. x lies in G, so x ↦ c_n|p_x u|² is a ν-a.e. limit of measurable functions. Hence it is ν-AEMeasurable (aemeasurable_of_tendsto_metrizable_ae'). Dividing by c_n > 0, x ↦ |p_x u|² is ν-AEMeasurable for every u ∈ ℝ^P.
8. Polarization. p_x is self-adjoint and idempotent, so ⟨p_x u, w⟩ = ⟨p_x u, p_x w⟩ = (|p_x(u + w)|² − |p_x(u − w)|²)/4. Hence x ↦ ⟨p_x u, w⟩ is ν-AEMeasurable for all u, w.
9. Assembly.
 (a) For every x, p_x = Σ_{a,b} ⟨p_x e_a, e_b⟩ L_{ab}, with the constant maps L_{ab} ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), L_{ab}(v) := ⟨e_a, v⟩e_b. This holds because p_x v = Σ_b ⟨p_x v, e_b⟩e_b and v = Σ_a ⟨e_a, v⟩e_a.
 (b) A finite sum of ν-AEMeasurable real functions times constant vectors of the normed space L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) (Borel σ-algebra) is ν-AEMeasurable. So x ↦ p_x = (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection is ν-AEMeasurable, hence R.measure-AEMeasurable by step 0.
proof_key_steps: μ_R ≪ ν = Hⁿ⌞M, and ν is σ-finite because U is open and θ ≥ 1 is locally integrable; the case n = 0 is trivial.
For f_u(y) = max(1 − |y|², 0)⟨u, y⟩², ∫_Q f_u dHⁿ = c_n|p_Q u|² for every n-plane Q, with c_n > 0.
x ↦ ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f_u dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫ f_u(λ⁻¹(y − x)) dν(y) is measurable (Tonelli); at a.e. x it tends to c_n|p_x u|² as λ = 1/(k+1) → 0.
Polarization and a basis expansion give AEMeasurable x ↦ p_x, first for ν and then for μ_R.

Source: steps 1–3 of the selected node's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2–3.4 and 3.16–3.17) for one ball. Provenance (not a proof step): the declaration is already comparator-accepted (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.mean_curvature_monotonicity-a1.exp_monotonicity-a1, candidate commit 81933e8). The proof below is adapted from its accepted proof and made self-contained by proving the first-variation integral formula inline in step 3(a). Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.6 (chapter-04.txt lines 215–312) and 3.14–3.17 (lines 370–430). The first range gives radial vector fields γ(r)(x − ξ), the formula div_M = nγ + rγ'(1 − |∇^⊥r|²) and the I, J identity; the second treats bounded generalized mean curvature. We use Simon's sign convention δV(X) = −∫X·H and prove the stated form directly, with open balls and e^{κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(z)) nondecreasing. Open balls arise because the cutoffs increase to the indicator of (−∞, 1).
Notation. μ := R.measure, M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x with orthogonal projection p_x, and ϱ(x) := |x − z|.
0. Preliminaries.
 (a) κ ≥ 0, since 0 ≤ ‖H(z)‖ ≤ κ.
 (b) μ(closedBall(z, r)) < ∞. The set closedBall(z, r) is compact, closed and contained in U, so μ(closedBall(z, r)) = ∫⁻_{M∩closedBall(z, r)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
 (c) For μ-a.e. x, finrank T_x = n, and hence trace(p_x) = n. By R.orients, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x admits Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q; then T_x is such a Q (definition of approxTangentPlane), so finrank T_x = n. Moreover μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M.
 (d) If r ≤ 0, there are no σ, ρ with 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ r. So assume r > 0.
1. Cutoffs. Let g(t) := 0 for t ≤ 0, g(t) := 3t² − 2t³ for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, and g(t) := 1 for t ≥ 1. Then g is C¹ (g' = 6t − 6t² on [0, 1] vanishes at 0 and 1), nondecreasing, and [0, 1]-valued. For ε ∈ (0, 1) let γ(t) := g((1 − t)/ε). Then γ is C¹, γ' ≤ 0, |γ'| ≤ 3/(2ε), 0 ≤ γ ≤ 1, γ(t) = 1 for t ≤ 1 − ε, and γ(t) = 0 for t ≥ 1. Any other C¹ nondecreasing g with g = 0 on (−∞, 0] and g = 1 on [1, ∞) works equally well, for example Mathlib's Real.smoothTransition; then the bound on |γ'| becomes sup|g'|/ε.
2. Radial fields. For s > 0 put φ_s(x) := γ(ϱ(x)/s) and X_s(x) := φ_s(x)(x − z).
 (a) φ_s and X_s are C¹: on ℝ^P ∖ {z}, ϱ is C^∞; on ball(z, (1 − ε)s), φ_s ≡ 1 and X_s(x) = x − z.
 (b) φ_s(x) ≠ 0 implies ϱ(x) < s. So tsupport X_s ⊆ closedBall(z, s), which is compact. For 0 < s < r, tsupport X_s ⊆ ball(z, r) ⊆ U.
 (c) Divergence. For x with finrank T_x = n, div_M X_s(x) = nφ_s(x) + ψ_s(x)q(x). Here ψ_s(x) := (ϱ(x)/s)γ'(ϱ(x)/s), q(x) := |p_x(x − z)|²/ϱ(x)² for x ≠ z, and q(z) := 0.
  - For x ≠ z: DX_s(x)v = φ_s(x)v + (γ'(ϱ/s)/(sϱ))⟨x − z, v⟩(x − z). Since trace(p_x) = n and the trace of p_x ∘ (v ↦ ⟨a, v⟩a) is ⟨a, p_x a⟩ = |p_x a|², we get div_M X_s(x) = nφ_s(x) + (γ'(ϱ/s)/(sϱ))|p_x(x − z)|² = nφ_s(x) + ψ_s(x)q(x).
  - At x = z: DX_s(z) = I, so div_M X_s(z) = n = nφ_s(z) + ψ_s(z)q(z), because φ_s(z) = 1 and ψ_s(z) = 0.
 (d) ψ_s is continuous, ψ_s ≤ 0, and ψ_s(x) = 0 unless (1 − ε)s < ϱ(x) < s. Also 0 ≤ q ≤ 1, since |p_x a| ≤ |a|, and q is μ-AEMeasurable by the AEMeasurable hypothesis on p_x.
3. First variation inequality. Let 0 < s < r and I(s) := ∫ φ_s dμ.
 (a) By definition (IMRep.firstVariation), R.firstVariation X_s = ∫_M θ(x)·div_M X_s(x) dHⁿ(x), where div_M X_s(x) = tangentialDivergence n M X_s x = trace(p_x ∘ DX_s(x)). θ is measurable (R.measurable_mult) with values in ℕ ⊆ ℝ≥0, and μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. So the density formula for Bochner integrals (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul) gives ∫ f dμ = ∫ θ(x)·f(x) d(Hⁿ⌞M)(x) = ∫_M θ f dHⁿ for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Both sides vanish together when f is not integrable, so no integrability is needed. With f = div_M X_s this is R.firstVariation X_s = ∫ div_M X_s dμ. By 2(c) and 0(c), div_M X_s = nφ_s + ψ_s q μ-a.e., so ∫ div_M X_s dμ = ∫ (nφ_s + ψ_s q) dμ (integral_congr_ae).
 (b) φ_s, ψ_s q and φ_s⟨x − z, H⟩ are bounded and AEStronglyMeasurable, and they vanish off closedBall(z, s), which has finite measure. So they are integrable.
 (c) The hypothesis applied to X_s gives nI(s) + ∫ψ_s q dμ = −∫ φ_s⟨x − z, H⟩ dμ.
 (d) ψ_s ≤ 0 and q ≤ 1 give ψ_s q ≥ ψ_s. On {φ_s ≠ 0}, |⟨x − z, H(x)⟩| ≤ ϱ(x)κ ≤ sκ. Hence
  (★) nI(s) + ∫ψ_s dμ ≤ κ s I(s).
4. Differentiability of I.
 (a) For each x, s ↦ φ_s(x) is differentiable on (0, ∞) with derivative −(ϱ(x)/s²)γ'(ϱ(x)/s) = −ψ_s(x)/s.
 (b) For s in a compact interval [a, b] ⊆ (0, r), this derivative is 0 unless ϱ(x) < s ≤ b, and it is bounded by (b/a²)·sup|γ'|. The dominating function (b/a²)·sup|γ'|·1_{closedBall(z, b)} is μ-integrable by 0(b).
 (c) By differentiation under the integral sign (hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le), I is differentiable on (0, r) with sI'(s) = −∫ψ_s dμ.
 (d) I is continuous on (0, r] by dominated convergence: s ↦ φ_s(x) is continuous, and |φ_s| ≤ 1_{closedBall(z, r)} for s ≤ r.
5. Monotonicity.
 (a) Let F(s) := e^{κs}s^{−n}I(s) for s ∈ (0, r]. By (★) and step 4, nI(s) − sI'(s) ≤ κsI(s) on (0, r). So F'(s) = e^{κs}s^{−n−1}(κsI(s) + sI'(s) − nI(s)) ≥ 0 there.
 (b) F is continuous on (0, r]. By the mean value theorem (monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg on the convex set (0, r], whose interior is (0, r)), F is nondecreasing on (0, r]. So for 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ r:
  (★★) e^{κσ}σ^{−n}∫γ(ϱ/σ) dμ ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}∫γ(ϱ/ρ) dμ.
6. Removing the cutoff.
 (a) Apply (★★) with ε = ε_j := 1/(j + 2), writing γ_j for the corresponding cutoff.
 (b) For every t: if t ≥ 1 then γ_j(t) = 0; if t < 1 then (1 − t)/ε_j ≥ 1 for large j, so γ_j(t) = 1. Hence γ_j(ϱ(x)/s) → 1_{ball(z, s)}(x) for every x and every s > 0. Also |γ_j(ϱ/s)| ≤ 1_{closedBall(z, r)} for s ≤ r.
 (c) By dominated convergence, ∫γ_j(ϱ/s) dμ → μ(ball(z, s)) for s ∈ {σ, ρ}.
 (d) Passing to the limit in (★★) gives e^{κσ}σ^{−n}μ(ball(z, σ)) ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}μ(ball(z, ρ)) as real numbers; both measures are finite by 0(b).
7. Extended reals. For s ∈ {σ, ρ}, μ(ball(z, s)) < ∞ and e^{κs}/s^n ≥ 0, so ENNReal.ofReal(e^{κs}/s^n)·μ(ball(z, s)) = ENNReal.ofReal(e^{κs}s^{−n}·μ(ball(z, s)).toReal). ENNReal.ofReal is monotone, so step 6 gives the claim.

The first variation hypothesis, together with q ≤ 1, ψ_s ≤ 0 and |⟨x − z, H⟩| ≤ κs, gives nI − sI' ≤ κsI.
(e^{κs}s^{−n}I(s))' ≥ 0 on (0, r), and continuity on (0, r] makes it nondecreasing on (0, r].
As ε ↓ 0, I(s) → μ_R(B_s(z)) by dominated convergence; then transfer the inequality to [0, ∞].

 - Define H := 1_S·H₁, i.e. H(x) := H₁(x) for x ∈ S and H(x) := 0 for x ∉ S (Set.indicator).
 - H is strongly measurable, as the indicator of a measurable set times a strongly measurable function (StronglyMeasurable.indicator). In particular H is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
3. (Global bound.) Let x ∈ ℝ^P. If x ∈ S, then ‖H(x)‖ = ‖H₁(x)‖ ≤ Λ. If x ∉ S, then ‖H(x)‖ = ‖0‖ = 0 ≤ Λ. So ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x.

 - Let t ∈ (0, ρ). By (I2), the left side equals ofReal(1/t^n)·m(B_t(z)).

subproblems.title: An approximate tangent plane forces unit Hⁿ-density on closed balls (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P, and s > 0 with H^n(M ∩ B̄_s(x)) < ∞, where H^n = μHE[n]. Suppose Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4, as formalized by HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q: dim Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0. Here η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) (blowUpMap), and the integrals are Bochner integrals for H^n restricted to the indicated sets. Then H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1 in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0. Here B̄_ρ(x) is the closed ball, ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n, and the quotient is taken in [0, ∞] with ρ^n entered via ENNReal.ofReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → μHE[n] (M ∩ closedBall x s) ≠ ∞ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => μHE[n] (M ∩ closedBall x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (not a proof step): this declaration is already comparator-accepted (node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.unweighted_density_one-a1, candidate commit dbef2c1), and the self-contained proof below is its accepted proof. In the selected node it supplies the unweighted density 1 of Hⁿ⌞M behind "Θ ≥ 1 μ-a.e." in step 7 of the supplied proof. Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 95-101), with Definition 1.4 at lines 77-84. In Definition 1.4 one chooses f with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f ≡ 1 on B_1(0) and f ≡ 0 off B_{1+ε}(0), and lets ε ↓ 0; this gives lim_{ρ↓0} (ω_nρ^n)^{-1} H^n(M ∩ B_ρ(x)) = 1. A second cut-off from inside gives the matching lower bound. Only closed balls are needed. The finiteness of H^n(M ∩ B̄_s(x)) is part of the standing hypothesis of Definition 1.4; it makes the Bochner integrals in the hypothesis genuine for small r. The proof covers n = 0 (ℝ^0 is a point and ω_0 = 1) without a separate case. If n > P, no subspace Q has dimension n, so the hypothesis cannot hold.

Notation: H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P; ω := unitBallVolume n, and w is ω as a real number. For r > 0, η_r := η_{x,r} = blowUpMap x r, ν_r := H^n⌞η_r(M), and μ_Q := H^n⌞Q. All balls are closed.

1. (ω_n.) ω = vol(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝ^n) is positive, being the measure of a nonempty open set (measure_ball_pos), and finite (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence w > 0 and ω = ofReal(w).

2. (Plane balls.) Since dim Q = n, reindexing an orthonormal basis of Q by Fin n gives a linear isometry ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P with range Q. For t ≥ 0, ι(B̄_t(0)) = Q ∩ B̄_t(0), because |ι v| = |v| and ι maps onto Q. Three facts compute this measure:
- H^n is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image);
- H^n equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume);
- vol(B̄_t(0)) = t^n vol(B_1(0)) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall, with finrank ℝ^n = n).
Hence μ_Q(B̄_t(0)) = H^n(Q ∩ B̄_t(0)) = ω·t^n. This is finite, with real value w t^n.

3. (Scaling.) Let r > 0 and A ⊆ ℝ^P. Then η_r(A) = r^{-1}·(A − x). The translation y ↦ y − x is an isometry, and H^n(cS) = |c|^n H^n(S) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). So H^n(η_r(A)) = r^{-n} H^n(A). Moreover |η_r(z)| ≤ t ⟺ dist(z, x) ≤ tr, so η_r(M) ∩ B̄_t(0) = η_r(M ∩ B̄_{tr}(x)). Hence
 ν_r(B̄_t(0)) = H^n(η_r(M) ∩ B̄_t(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(M ∩ B̄_{tr}(x)).
In particular ν_r(B̄_t(0)) < ∞ whenever tr ≤ s, by monotonicity and the hypothesis H^n(M ∩ B̄_s(x)) < ∞.

4. (Cut-off functions.) For 0 < a < b let g_{a,b}(y) := max{0, min{1, (b − |y|)/(b − a)}}.
- g_{a,b} is continuous.
- It vanishes when |y| ≥ b, so its support lies in the compact ball B̄_b(0) and g_{a,b} ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
- 0 ≤ g_{a,b} ≤ 1, and g_{a,b} = 1 when |y| ≤ a.
Consequently 1_{B̄_a(0)} ≤ g_{a,b} ≤ 1_{B̄_b(0)} pointwise.

5. (Integrability.) Let ν' be a measure on ℝ^P with ν'(B̄_t(0)) < ∞. Then 1_{B̄_t(0)} is ν'-integrable, and by domination so is every continuous f with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_t(0)}. By steps 2-3 this applies to ν_r when tr ≤ s, to μ_Q for all t, and to the cut-offs of step 4. For such f, ∫ f dν' and ∫ 1_{B̄_t(0)} dν' = ν'(B̄_t(0)) (as a real number; integral_indicator_one) are genuine finite integrals, and integral_mono compares them.

6. (Normalised mass.) For r > 0 put a(r) := r^{-n}·H^n(M ∩ B̄_r(x)). This is a real number since H^n(M ∩ B̄_r(x)) < ∞ for r ≤ s. By step 3 with t = 1, the real value of ν_r(B̄_1(0)) is a(r).

7. (a(r) → w.) It suffices to show that, as r → 0 within (0, ∞), eventually c < a(r) for each c < w, and eventually a(r) < c for each c > w.
(i) Let c < w.
- The map ε ↦ w(1 − ε)^n is continuous with value w at 0. Pick ε ∈ (0, 1) with c < w(1 − ε)^n and let f₁ := g_{1−ε,1}.
- By steps 2, 4 and 5, ∫_Q f₁ dH^n ≥ ∫ 1_{B̄_{1−ε}(0)} dμ_Q = w(1 − ε)^n > c.
- By the hypothesis applied to f₁, ∫_{η_r(M)} f₁ dH^n → ∫_Q f₁ dH^n, so eventually ∫_{η_r(M)} f₁ dH^n > c.
- For 0 < r ≤ s/2 (so 1·r ≤ s), f₁ ≤ 1_{B̄_1(0)} gives ∫_{η_r(M)} f₁ dH^n ≤ ν_r(B̄_1(0)) = a(r) (steps 5 and 6).
Hence eventually a(r) > c.
(ii) Let c > w.
- Pick ε ∈ (0, 1) with w(1 + ε)^n < c and let f₂ := g_{1,1+ε}.
- ∫_Q f₂ dH^n ≤ ∫ 1_{B̄_{1+ε}(0)} dμ_Q = w(1 + ε)^n < c, so eventually ∫_{η_r(M)} f₂ dH^n < c.
- For 0 < r ≤ s/2 we have (1 + ε)r ≤ 2r ≤ s, so f₂ is ν_r-integrable (step 5).
- 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ f₂ gives a(r) = ν_r(B̄_1(0)) ≤ ∫_{η_r(M)} f₂ dH^n.
Hence eventually a(r) < c.
By the order-topology characterisation (tendsto_order), a(r) → w as r ↓ 0.

8. (Back to [0, ∞].) Let 0 < ρ ≤ s. Write H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = ofReal(m), where m is its (finite) real value; also ω = ofReal(w) and ω·ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(wρ^n) with wρ^n > 0. Then
 H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω·ofReal(ρ^n)) = ofReal(m/(wρ^n)) = ofReal(a(ρ)/w)
(ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos). Since a(ρ)/w → w/w = 1 and ofReal is continuous, ofReal(a(ρ)/w) → 1. The two functions agree on (0, s], a right-neighbourhood of 0, so the quotient tends to 1 as ρ ↓ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: H^n(Q ∩ B̄_t(0)) = ω_n t^n, via a linear isometry ℝ^n ≅ Q and H^n = Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n.
H^n(η_{x,r}(M) ∩ B̄_t(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(M ∩ B̄_{tr}(x)), which is finite when tr ≤ s.
The radial cut-offs in C_c satisfy g_{1−ε,1} ≤ 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ g_{1,1+ε}. So a(r) = r^{-n}H^n(M ∩ B̄_r(x)) lies between the blow-up integrals of the two cut-offs.
Tangent-plane convergence and ∫_Q bounds of ω_n(1∓ε)^n give a(r) → ω_n. Converting to the [0,∞] quotient gives the limit 1.

subproblems.title: Closed-ball density limits give the same open-ball density limit (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let ν be any Borel measure on ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P and θ ∈ [0, ∞]. Write ω_n = unitBallVolume n (the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n) and, for ρ > 0, c(ρ) = ω_n·ρ^n ∈ [0, ∞], with ρ^n entered via ENNReal.ofReal. If ν(B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0, then ν(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ as ρ ↓ 0. Here B̄_ρ(x) and B_ρ(x) are the closed and open balls, and quotients are taken in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (θ : ℝ≥0∞), Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => ν (closedBall x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 θ) → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => ν (ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 θ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (not a proof step): this declaration is already comparator-accepted (node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.closed_to_open_ball_density-a1, candidate commit c3ca64f), and the self-contained proof below is its accepted proof. Source: Simon Ch. 1, 3.1-3.2 (chapter-01.txt lines 561-592) observes that the n-dimensional densities may be computed with closed balls B_ρ(x) or with open balls. The frozen contract's docstring for HasMassDensity says the same: open and closed balls give the same limit. The argument is the sandwich B̄_{tρ}(x) ⊆ B_ρ(x) ⊆ B̄_ρ(x), followed by t ↑ 1. Here it is carried out in the order topology of [0, ∞], which also covers θ = ∞.

Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n and c(ρ) := ω·ofReal(ρ^n). Let g(ρ) := ν(B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) and h(ρ) := ν(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ), all in [0, ∞]. By hypothesis g(ρ) → θ as ρ → 0 within (0, ∞). Below, eventually always refers to ρ → 0 within (0, ∞). By the characterisation of convergence in the order topology of [0, ∞] (tendsto_order), it suffices to prove:
- (U) for every b > θ, eventually h(ρ) < b;
- (L) for every a < θ, eventually h(ρ) > a.

1. (Upper bound (U).) For every ρ, B_ρ(x) ⊆ B̄_ρ(x), so ν(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ν(B̄_ρ(x)). Dividing both by the same c(ρ) gives h(ρ) ≤ g(ρ). Given b > θ, eventually g(ρ) < b because g → θ. Hence eventually h(ρ) ≤ g(ρ) < b.

2. (Choice of a dilation factor.) Let a < θ.
- As t → 1 from below, ofReal(t^n) → ofReal(1) = 1, by continuity of t ↦ t^n and of ofReal.
- Hence ofReal(t^n)·θ → 1·θ = θ. Multiplication by the constant θ is continuous at the limit 1 because 1 ≠ 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const).
- Since a < θ, eventually (as t → 1⁻) a < ofReal(t^n)·θ; also eventually t ∈ (0, 1). Pick such a t.
Put τ := ofReal(t^n). Since 0 < t, τ ∈ (0, ∞), i.e. τ ≠ 0 and τ ≠ ∞. From a < τ·θ we get a/τ < θ (ENNReal.div_lt_iff).

3. (Rescaled ratio.) The map ρ ↦ tρ sends (0, ∞) into (0, ∞) and tends to 0 as ρ → 0, so it tends to 0 within (0, ∞). Composing with g → θ gives g(tρ) → θ as ρ → 0 within (0, ∞). Since a/τ < θ, eventually g(tρ) > a/τ.

4. (Scaling identity.) Let ρ > 0. Then (tρ)^n = t^n ρ^n with t^n ≥ 0, so ofReal((tρ)^n) = τ·ofReal(ρ^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul) and c(tρ) = ω·τ·ofReal(ρ^n). Two facts finish the computation:
- (ω·ofReal(ρ^n)·τ)^{-1} = (ω·ofReal(ρ^n))^{-1}·τ^{-1} (ENNReal.mul_inv, valid as τ ≠ 0, ∞);
- τ^{-1}·τ = 1 (ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel).
Together they give g(tρ)·τ = ν(B̄_{tρ}(x))/c(ρ).

5. (Lower bound (L).) Let ρ > 0 with g(tρ) > a/τ; this holds eventually by step 3. Since 0 < t < 1, tρ < ρ, so B̄_{tρ}(x) ⊆ B_ρ(x). Therefore
 a = (a/τ)·τ < g(tρ)·τ = ν(B̄_{tρ}(x))/c(ρ) ≤ ν(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) = h(ρ).
The four relations use, in order:
- (a/τ)·τ = a (ENNReal.div_mul_cancel, τ ≠ 0, ∞);
- strict monotonicity of multiplication by τ ∈ (0, ∞) (ENNReal.mul_lt_mul_iff_left);
- step 4;
- monotonicity of ν.
Hence eventually h(ρ) > a.

6. Steps 1 and 5 give (U) and (L) for all b > θ and all a < θ. Hence h(ρ) → θ as ρ ↓ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: B_ρ(x) ⊆ B̄_ρ(x) gives h ≤ g, hence the upper bound.
For a < θ, choose t ∈ (0,1) with a < t^n θ, using t^n θ → θ as t ↑ 1.
B̄_{tρ}(x) ⊆ B_ρ(x) and c(tρ) = t^n c(ρ) give h(ρ) ≥ t^n g(tρ) > a eventually.
Conclude by the order-topology characterisation of convergence in [0, ∞].

subproblems.title: Lower bound 1 for every ball-density limit of an integer multiplicity weight at almost every point (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with weight μ := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then the following holds for μ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P. Whenever θ₀ ∈ ℝ and μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → ofReal(θ₀) in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0, θ₀ ≥ 1. Here ω_n = unitBallVolume n and B_ρ(x) = ball x ρ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ θ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => R.measure (ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (ENNReal.ofReal θ)) → 1 ≤ θ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (not a proof step): this declaration is comparator-accepted (node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.monotonicity-a1.ae_density_lower_bound-a1, candidate commit b59dbf9, isolated comparator passed) and is reused here at its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is the one approved in the decomposition audit (v2) of root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.monotonicity-a1, whose supplied proof has the same numbered steps 0–7 as the selected node's; it is the proof from which the declaration was formalized.
Source: the first half of step 7 of the selected node's supplied proof ("Θ ≥ 1 μ-a.e."), i.e. Simon Ch. 4, 3.13 and the sentence after it (chapter-04.txt lines 350–364), with Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 95–101). Only a lower bound is needed. So instead of Θⁿ(μ, x) = θ(x) (Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 with Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2)), we use θ ≥ 1 and the unit density of the unweighted measure Hⁿ⌞M, which is given by the siblings closed_ball_unit_density and open_ball_density.
Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ, ω_n := unitBallVolume n, B_t(z) := ball z t.
1. (Reduction to ν.) μ ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). So every property that holds for ν-a.e. x holds for μ-a.e. x (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). It suffices to prove the claim for ν-a.e. x.
2. (Good points.) M is Borel, so ν-a.e. x lies in M (ae_restrict_mem). By the field R.orients, for ν-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. Both properties hold simultaneously for ν-a.e. x.
3. (Weight versus area.) For every Borel A, ν(A) ≤ μ(A). Indeed μ(A) = ∫⁻_A θ dν (withDensity_apply). θ is ℕ-valued and positive on M (R.mult_pos), and ν-a.e. point lies in M, so θ ≥ 1 ν-a.e. Hence μ(A) ≥ ∫⁻_A 1 dν = ν(A).
4. (Local finiteness.) Fix x as in step 2, with x ∈ M and a subspace Q. Fix θ₀ ∈ ℝ with μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → ofReal(θ₀) as ρ ↓ 0; we must show θ₀ ≥ 1. Since x ∈ M ⊆ U (R.carrier_subset) and U is open, there is s > 0 with closedBall x s ⊆ U. closedBall x s is compact, and θ ≥ 1 on M, so Hⁿ(M ∩ closedBall x s) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ closedBall x s} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{M ∩ closedBall x s} θ dHⁿ < ∞. The last bound is the field R.locallyIntegrable_mult for K = closedBall x s.
5. (Unit density of ν.)
 - By the sibling closed_ball_unit_density, applied to M, x, Q and s (using step 4 and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q), Hⁿ(M ∩ closedBall x ρ)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0.
 - Closed balls are Borel, so ν(closedBall x ρ) = Hⁿ(closedBall x ρ ∩ M) = Hⁿ(M ∩ closedBall x ρ) for every ρ (Measure.restrict_apply). Hence ν(closedBall x ρ)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → 1.
 - By the sibling open_ball_density, applied to ν, x and the limit 1, ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0.
6. (Comparison and conclusion.) By step 3 with A = B_ρ(x), ν(B_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) for every ρ. Division by the same element of [0, ∞] is monotone (ENNReal.div_le_div_right), so ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) for every ρ. The left side tends to 1 by step 5, and the right side tends to ofReal(θ₀) by assumption. The filter ρ ↓ 0 is nontrivial, so 1 ≤ ofReal(θ₀) (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'). Hence θ₀ ≥ 1 (ENNReal.one_le_ofReal). This holds for every such θ₀ and every x in the ν-full set of step 2, so by step 1 the claim holds for μ-a.e. x.
proof_key_steps: μ_R ≪ ν = Hⁿ⌞M, and ν-a.e. x lies in M and has an approximate tangent plane Q.
θ ≥ 1 on M gives ν ≤ μ_R on Borel sets and Hⁿ(M ∩ closedBall x s) < ∞ for small s (locallyIntegrable_mult).
closed_ball_unit_density and open_ball_density give ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1.
Comparing ν ≤ μ_R along ρ ↓ 0 gives 1 ≤ ofReal θ₀, i.e. θ₀ ≥ 1.

1. (Reduction to Θ.) Let y ∈ spt T and θ ∈ ℝ with HasMassDensity T y θ. Since spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T) ⊆ U (GeometricCurrentOn.support_subset_domain), y ∈ U, and (d) gives HasMassDensity T y (Θ(y)). The function ρ ↦ M_{B_ρ(y)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) therefore tends both to ofReal(θ) and to ofReal(Θ(y)) along 𝓝[>]0. This filter is nontrivial and [0, ∞] is Hausdorff, so ofReal(θ) = ofReal(Θ(y)) (tendsto_nhds_unique). Both θ ≥ 0 and Θ(y) ≥ 0 by the first conjunct of HasMassDensity, so θ = Θ(y) (ENNReal.ofReal_eq_ofReal_iff). It remains to show Θ(y) ≥ 1.
2. (A ball on which Θ < 1.) Suppose, for contradiction, that Θ(y) < 1. By (e) at y ∈ U, Θ(z) < 1 for all z in some 𝓝[U] y-neighbourhood of y. Since U is open and y ∈ U, 𝓝[U] y = 𝓝 y (nhdsWithin_eq_nhds). So there is ε > 0 such that every z ∈ B_ε(y) satisfies Θ(z) < 1 and z ∈ U.
3. (No good point in the ball.) Let G be the set of x with the property in (c): for every θ' ∈ ℝ, if μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → ofReal(θ') as ρ ↓ 0, then θ' ≥ 1. By (c), μ(ℝ^P ∖ G) = 0 (ae_iff). Let z ∈ B_ε(y); then z ∈ U and Θ(z) < 1.
 - For 0 < ρ < ε − dist(z, y), B_ρ(z) ⊆ B_ε(y) ⊆ U by the triangle inequality, and B_ρ(z) is open. So by (a), M_{B_ρ(z)}(T) = μ(B_ρ(z)).
 - So the functions ρ ↦ M_{B_ρ(z)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) and ρ ↦ μ(B_ρ(z))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) agree on (0, ε − dist(z, y)), which belongs to 𝓝[>]0.
 - By (d), the first function tends to ofReal(Θ(z)), hence so does the second (Tendsto.congr').
 - Since Θ(z) < 1, θ' := Θ(z) violates the property defining G, so z ∉ G.
 Hence B_ε(y) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ G.
4. (Contradiction.) By monotonicity of μ, μ(B_ε(y)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P ∖ G) = 0 (measure_mono_null). This contradicts (b) for y ∈ spt T and ε > 0. Therefore Θ(y) ≥ 1, and θ = Θ(y) ≥ 1.
